source.title: Some open problems of Ramsey minimal graphs.

accepted.question_text: Let F, G, and H be non-empty graphs, and write F → (G, H) to mean that every red-blue coloring of the edges of F contains either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but, for every edge e of F, the graph F − e fails to satisfy F − e → (G, H). Let ℜ(G, H) denote the set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs. For each integer t ≥ 6, classify all 2-connected graphs in ℜ(2K2, tK2), where 2K2 is the matching consisting of two disjoint edges and tK2 is the matching consisting of t disjoint edges.

evidence.quote: F, G, and H, say that F → (G, H) if whenever the edges of F are 2-colored, say with red and blue, there is either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is called Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but for any edge e ∈ E(F), we have (F - e) ↛ (G, H). The set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs, the topic of this note, is denoted by ℜ(G, H).
Problem 1. For each t ≥ 6, characterize all 2-connected graphs in ℜ(2K2, tK2).
